Checkbox state and dropdown values are read back off the page rather than echoed from the request. Password inputs are never filled, only named. Verified live on https://www.selenium.dev/selenium/web/web-form.html: five dictated labels matched, screenshot matches the manifest, page never left web-form.html.

entries.summary: Implement adaptive duplex behavior: when downlink audio is playing, reduce or pause uplink capture/encoding to avoid LTE contention; resume capture after playback. Add LED state to indicate “receiving” vs “recording.”
entries.note: Adaptive duplex uplink in firmware/nrf9160 (src/main.c + audio_opus.c/h). While downlink audio is playing (dl_jitter_fill>0 plus a 300 ms hangover): DUCK halves the uplink Opus target via new pendant_opus_stream_set_bitrate() (16000 -> 8000 bps), and HOLD stops feeding the encoder once the 7 KiB uplink FIFO passes 60% fill (releases below 40%, or immediately when playback ends), reserving ~2.8 KiB for the user's next question. Chose duck-not-mute because barge-in is server-side: a fully paused uplink would make the agent uninterruptible. New counters duck_ms and uplink_held added to the 'Conversation stats:' printk. RAM before 202676 B (95.78%) / FLASH 382952 B (64.93%); RAM after 202700 B (95.79%) / FLASH 383312 B (64.99%) — +24 B RAM, +360 B flash, 8908 B headroom left. FLASHED to the DK and verified running: 61 s duplex conversation, max_loop_ms=22, tx_starved=0, mic_drops=0, uplink_drops=0, fifo_left=293, new fields print (duck_ms=0 uplink_held=0). NOT YET EXERCISED: that run had decoded_packets=0 (agent never spoke, silent room), so the duck/hold path itself is unverified on hardware — it only proves the adaptation does not engage spuriously. Needs a conversation with real speech to confirm.

entries.summary: Add a server-side browser harness (Cloudflare Browser Run) so the relay can perform read-only web tasks without requiring the Mac to be online, with strict allowlists and output sanitization.
entries.note: cloud-relay/serverBrowser.js + serverBrowser.test.js (35 tests, all pass). Cloudflare Browser Run Quick Actions: readPublicPage() prefers the Workers env.BROWSER binding (no token in-Worker, needs compat_date >= 2026-03-24; ours is 2026-07-31) and falls back to REST (CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID/CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN) for the node relay. wrangler.jsonc now declares the browser binding; dry-run confirms 'env.BROWSER -> Browser Run' and the module bundles for workerd. VERIFIED LIVE against account 137c3d31 with the existing wrangler OAuth token (scope 'browser (write)'): example.com read in 2.25s browser-time, docs page sanitized+truncated, private/loopback URLs refused before any egress. PLAN REALITY (measured, not read): this account is Workers FREE, so Browser Run allows 1 Quick Action per 10s (observed 429 + Retry-After: 10 on a back-to-back call) and 10 browser-minutes/day. Workers Paid lifts that to 10/s and unmetered. No upgrade is required to ship; it only bounds throughput. Read-only public web is a CAPABILITY boundary, not a permission gate: the edge browser holds no owner cookies and is on no owner network, so logins and LAN pages route to browser_run_actions (Mac extension) - the result carries a hint saying exactly that, plus a login-wall heuristic. Output sanitization: front-matter title lifted, zero-width/bidi-override chars stripped (hidden-instruction vector), control chars removed, base64 data: URIs collapsed, 12k char cap, results flagged untrusted:true. NOT WIRED: openaiRealtimeVoice.js/server.js/jobs.js were owned by a concurrent agent. The exact 3-file wiring patch (openaiRealtimeVoice.js import + READ_WEB_PAGE_TOOL as the 6th tool + read_web_page dispatch branch; openaiRealtimeVoice.test.js tool-list assertion; fleetContext.js routing line + capability line) is in the report; verified with git apply --check and by running the full 135-test suite against a wired copy - all pass.

entries.summary: Add transactional desktop jobs: each plan has a preview, stable job/action IDs, preconditions (expected app/path/hash), checkpoints, result receipts, and compensating undo where possible. On retry, skip completed action IDs rather than replaying clicks or shell commands. Prefer accessibility selectors and declarative APIs over coordinates.
entries.note: Built the receipt/undo half only. NO gates, NO approval prompts, NO preconditions — nothing added here can refuse or skip an action, per owner policy. New local-agent/actionReceipts.js; executor.js now wraps every dispatch: observeBeforeAction(action) runs first (pure observation, swallows all errors, its verdict is never read), then buildActionReceipt() attaches a receipt to every result — successful or failed. Receipt carries: content-addressed actionId (stable across a re-run of the same plan; positional index would not be, because the orchestrator hands the executor one action at a time), unique receiptId, effect read|write, what was touched (paths, urls, apps, shell commands, email recipients, clipboard, settings with before/after), duration, and an honest reversibility verdict with reversedBy or irreversibleReason. Reversibility now lives in ONE place: undo.js imports describeReversibility() so the receipt the owner reads and the decision undo makes cannot disagree; jobs recorded before receipts existed fall back to the raw result fields, so old history stays undoable. COMPENSATING UNDO: observeBeforeAction snapshots any file a write_file/create_note/delete_path/copy_path/move_path is about to clobber into ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace/.undo (bounded at 8 MB; directories and oversize files are recorded as irreversible WITH the reason rather than silently half-copied). This makes delete_path — previously permanent — undoable, and fixes a real data-loss bug: undo used to answer 'yes, reversible' for a write_file that OVERWROTE an existing file and then reverse it by DELETING that file, destroying content the agent never wrote. Now it restores the exact prior bytes. Surfaced at GET /jobs (receipts per job), new GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts (counts + per-step undo verdict + snapshot vault path), and inside GET /ops/snapshot so the dashboard and relay see them too. describeUndoability now returns steps[] and irreversible[] with reasons, so 'why can't I undo this?' has an answer. Verified live end to end: overwrote a hand-written file via POST /execute, receipt showed reversible=true reversedBy='restore snapshot', POST /jobs/:id/undo restored the original content. Tests: actionReceipts.test.js (16); full suite 499/499.

entries.summary: Enable a bounded audio-retention sweeper and per-job deletion controls: default to short retention for generated briefings, delete expired R2 objects and D1 pointers idempotently, and expose a dashboard ‘delete now’ action. Keep owner-pinned items separate with an explicit expiry.
entries.note: NOTE RE-DERIVED 2026-08-07. The previous agent's 4,452-char patch plan was DESTROYED when this entry was set to "implementing": scripts/harness-ledger.mjs status --note overwrites the note, it does not append. Every claim below was re-verified against the live files today; the headline claim holds and is worse than it was stated. HEADLINE (TRUE): the sweeper cannot clear a backlog. audioRetention.js:171-175 lists with limit Math.min(Math.max(n,1),100) and passes no cursor; store/jobQuery.js:8 JOB_LIST_MAX_LIMIT = 100 clamps it again, so raising the local constant alone fixes nothing. Ordering is newest-first on both stores (store/d1Store.js:566 ORDER BY created_at DESC; store/memoryStore.js:166). The sweep therefore only ever inspects the 100 NEWEST audio_capture rows — the ones least likely to be expired — and repeated runs never advance the window. A keyset cursor already exists and is plumbed through listJobs({before}) (store/jobQuery.js:19-37, used at server.js:1893); sweepExpiredAudio simply never passes it. OTHER VERIFIED GAPS. (2) AUDIO_RETENTION_SWEEP_MAX_BATCH = 200 at audioRetention.js:32 is unreachable dead config given the 100 cap. (3) No scheduled invocation exists: cloudflare-worker/worker.js exports only fetch, wrangler.jsonc has no crons/triggers, and the sole caller is the manual route at server.js:2151. (4) Inert as shipped: wrangler.jsonc:34 sets AUDIO_RETENTION_SWEEP_ENABLED=false and server.js:2149 forces dryRun, so the deployed sweeper deletes nothing under any input. (5) Bindings are not threaded into either delete path: server.js:2151 and server.js:2834 call without bindings, and cloudflareBindings is only populated inside the Worker fetch handler — under plain Node deleteAudioCaptureObject short-circuits false (audioStorage.js:130-136), so the D1 pointer is cleared at audioRetention.js:141-147 while the R2 object is orphaned permanently, and the response still returns ok:true. (6) Non-atomic ordering: the R2 delete precedes the pointer clear, so an updateJob throw leaves a row addressing a deleted object. (7) In record mode with no store.deleteJob the object is already gone while the row keeps a stale audioRef; that branch has no test. (8) One R2 error aborts the whole sweep: audioRetention.js:195-204 is an unguarded loop with no per-item try/catch and no partial report. (9) NO owner-pin concept exists anywhere in cloud-relay — the entry's "keep owner-pinned items separate with an explicit expiry" is 0% implemented. (10) One global 30-day TTL (config.js:27-31, wrangler.jsonc:33); generated agent audio is an ordinary audio_capture row tagged role:reply (server.js:1075), so "short retention for generated briefings" is not implemented and there is no briefing concept in cloud-relay at all. (11) DELETE /v1/ops/history/:pipelineId/audio (server.js:1979-1995) never follows replyCaptureId, so deleting a run leaves the synthesized reply audio in R2 — and record mode destroys the only reference to it. (12) No dashboard reaches either delete route: src/ops/api.js has no audio DELETE and no retention call at all, so the "dashboard delete now action" does not exist in the frontend. (13) The read-only report at server.js:2115 hardcodes limit 100, so storedRecordings and expiredCount are structurally wrong past 100 captures. (14) The sweep report calls captures.length "scanned" (audioRetention.js:182,209), implying a full-corpus scan that never happened. NO DEFECT FOUND on clock/units: createdAt is ISO-8601 wherever written (jobs.js:20,34-35), parsed with Date.getTime (audioRetention.js:62) and compared against ms Date.now (audioRetention.js:78,86); maxAgeMs is milliseconds in config.js:27, in wrangler.jsonc:33 (2592000000 = 30d) and in the comparison alike. TEST GAPS: audioRetention.test.js never exercises a backlog >100 through a real store (the batch-cap test calls selectExpiredAudioCaptures on a plain array, bypassing listJobs, so gap 1 is invisible to the suite and gap 2 is asserted as correct), never makes an R2 delete throw, and always passes bindings explicitly — which is precisely what production does not do. cloud-relay/ was NOT edited. Left proposed.

entries.note: Built the inspect/act pair, NOT the confirmation half. local-agent/browserInspect.js + POST /browser/inspect, GET /browser/inspections[/:id], POST /browser/inspections/:id/act, action types browser_inspect / browser_inspect_act (both on the hands-free allowlist). inspect addresses a page, reads it, and returns findings as quote+citation (url, title, retrievedAt, locator) plus ONE proposed next step with its effect sentence and the evidence for choosing it — and does not act: the reading phase is handed an allow-set of navigate/list_tabs/read_page/snapshot, so click/type/select/press_key are unreachable from that code path, enforced in browserPage.runBrowserActions rather than by comment. A term that is not on the page comes back missing:true with a locator saying so, instead of a fabricated quote; nothing matching means proposal:null rather than a guessed click. act() re-snapshots and RE-LOCATES the element by selector, then name+role, then href — never by the stored ref, because the extension stamps refs e0,e1,... fresh per snapshot in DOM order, so a stale ref on a page that lazy-loaded a banner points at a different button (the owner reads 'Download invoice', the agent clicks 'Cancel subscription'). If the element is genuinely gone it fails; it never substitutes another. NOT BUILT, deliberately: the 'repeats the destination then waits for owner confirmation' clause and the 'continue only for that displayed proposal' token. That is the confirmation broker rejected in chg-75156244/chg-6a6fa4b6/chg-71ae0f60. browser_click, browser_type and browser_navigate are untouched and still execute immediately with no inspection required; inspect is an extra phase an agent may choose, not a checkpoint. 10 node:test cases including one asserting no confirmationToken/expiresAt/requiresApproval field exists. Live: extension online (Safari, 6 tabs) and browser_list_tabs verified through the bridge; the /browser/inspect round trip itself is UNVERIFIED live — two attempts were cut off by other subagents restarting the agent, and per the coordinator I stopped restarting it.

entries.note: local-agent/folderSweep.js: surveyFolder / planSweep / formatSweep / applySweep / undoSweep, plus GET /sweep/survey, POST /sweep/preview, GET /sweep[/:planId], POST /sweep/:planId/apply, POST /sweep/:planId/undo, and the sweep_folder_preview / _apply / _undo action types. Real classification, not a name-based guess: half-finished downloads (.crdownload/.part/.tmp/~$ and zero-byte files at least a day old, so nothing mid-write is touched), byte-identical duplicates (size + 64 KB sample to find candidates, then a full sha256 to settle it, capped at 256 MB above which the match is reported as unconfirmed and never proposed for deletion), stale installers (with an /Applications lookup so it can say "cursor is already installed"), stale files, and screenshots. Dispositions: delete / archive / file / flag / keep. Duplicates are only proposed for deletion when the bytes are proven identical AND the name reads as a copy ("report (1).pdf" beside "report.pdf"); anything that merely shares content is reported and left alone. Destinations are resolved to a free name at preview time, so nothing is ever overwritten and the path the owner reads is the path the file lands at. THE PREVIEW ON THE OWNER REAL DESKTOP, live through the running agent: 588 loose files, 556 screenshots and screen recordings totalling ~10 GB proposed into Screenshots/YYYY-MM/, 27 stale files into Archive/YYYY-MM/, 5 left alone. Nothing was applied. That preview also found a real bug: this Mac names screenshots in Traditional Chinese, and 30-odd files called "截圖 ..." were being filed as merely stale - SCREENSHOT_NAME now covers zh/ja/ko/es/fr/de/ru/nl as well as English, which is the sort of thing only real files tell you. NOT a gate: applySweep never asks anything, there is no token or expiry on a plan (a test asserts that), and move_path/delete_path still run immediately through /execute exactly as before. Apply takes a planId because "do what you showed me" is only meaningful if the thing applied is the thing shown; it re-checks every source against the recorded size and mtime and reports drift rather than substituting a fresh guess, and it runs through the ordinary executor so each item leaves a receipt and an undo-vault snapshot. 18 node:test cases.

entries.summary: Make every Mac plan two-phase by default: first return a concise preview with affected app/files/URLs and expected side effects, then execute only the safe subset automatically; preserve the owner’s current foreground app and use accessibility-targeted actions rather than stealing focus. Add a single spoken 'undo last plan' for supported reversible operations.
entries.note: Built the preview half; the "execute only the safe subset automatically" half is deliberately NOT built. local-agent/planPreview.js: foreseeAction/foreseePlan/formatPlanPreview. The idea is that a preview is the receipt an action has not written yet, so it imports from actionReceipts.js instead of re-deriving anything - touches come from buildActionReceipt with no result, which is the same describeTouched the real receipt uses a moment later, and the preview actionId IS the receipt actionId, so the line the owner reads and the line in history are joinable. It resolves "conditional" reversibility into a real answer while the file is still there: a delete of a 9 MB file reports "too large to snapshot, could not be undone" against the same SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES the vault will apply; a move onto an occupied name says it would replace something, before renameSync silently does. Surfaced two ways: POST /preview for any action list, and a preview field attached to the POST /plan response (affected apps/files/URLs, the undo story, and bulk:true as advice). Also a preview_plan action type. ADDITIVE ONLY: /plan returns the same plan it always did, /execute never reads the preview field, and there is no blocked/approved/requiresApproval/confirmationToken key anywhere - a test asserts their absence, since that is exactly how the rejected proposals worked. The other two clauses of the ask already shipped: foreground preservation is focusPolicy.js openArgs, and spoken "undo last plan" is POST /jobs/undo-last. Verified live before the restart freeze: POST /preview on a 3-step plan containing delete_path of ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace correctly reported bulk:true and "cannot be undone: only single files are snapshotted" - and the folder was still there afterwards. 7 node:test cases.

Every node writes typed facts, preferences, commitments, and task outcomes with provenance, confidence, sensitivity, expiry, and visibility scope; each surface requests a relevance-filtered context slice by task rather than receiving a giant static prompt. Add contradiction resolution and supersession, plus a nightly cheap-model compaction job.

Unify memory across surfaces: replace hand-written prompt sections per surface with a shared, versioned memory API that returns small, purpose-built summaries (profile, preferences, current projects, recent tasks) plus a citation trail. Add write paths with confidence and decay/TTL to prevent prompt bloat.

Introduce a unified, cross-node memory write API with schema (entities, events, preferences, tasks) and TTLs, plus a pruning policy. Replace hand-written per-surface prompt sections with retrieval-based context assembly.

Add a real scheduler: a Durable Object-backed job queue with delayed execution and recurring rules (cron-like). The relay can enqueue jobs, and a workers cron/alarm runner executes them, delegating to mac_delegate or server_browser_actions as needed. Include idempotency keys, retry with backoff, and cancellation.

Add a relay-owned durable work queue with retries and a receipt log, implemented as a Durable Object (or D1 + Durable Object alarms). The relay exposes enqueue/status endpoints, persists intent payloads, and emits receipts when downstream nodes complete. Jobs can be routed to Mac or server browser based on availability and task type.
Introduce a lightweight scheduler using Durable Object alarms or Cloudflare Cron to trigger queued jobs (summarize notes, send digests, retry failed uploads).

Add a browser-bridge self-healing lease protocol: each Safari heartbeat carries a device nonce, extension version, tab inventory, and last-applied command sequence; the Mac agent expires orphaned pending commands, replays only unacknowledged idempotent commands after reconnect, and emits a distinct stale/aborted result for commands that cannot safely replay. Add a local 'reconnect extension' diagnostic surfaced in the dashboard rather than leaving pendingCommands stranded.

entries.note: Shipped as the relay_job_status Realtime tool (7th tool in REALTIME_TOOLS), backed by the new cloud-relay/jobRecall.js. Note was empty before this; nothing to preserve. Voice path end to end: openaiRealtimeVoice.js answers the tool INSIDE the turn like web_search — it never sets state.actions, so a status question dispatches no Mac job — and both session call sites inject the lookup (cloud-relay/server.js /v1/pendant/command, cloud-relay/pendantConverse.js duplex WS). Deliberate: the relay already holds the Mac's returned result/error for every job it dispatched, it is in-process (no round trip inside a spoken turn), and it still answers when the Mac is asleep — which is exactly the case where 'your Mac never picked it up' is the true answer. local-agent /journal is richer per action but needs a live bridge round trip and is not in OPS_ALLOWED_PREFIXES. Terminal status with no result => 'unknown', and executed:false => 'failed' — the voiceRunForCapture bug (hardcoded success, silent runs reported completed) is covered by two regression tests. Approval gates report as awaiting_approval; queued past 60s reports as 'your Mac hasn't picked it up'. No approval gates or confirmation prompts added. entries.summary: Introduce a typed, minimal context service for the relay: given an utterance and a desired outcome (status query, dictation, mac task), return only relevant facts (device online state, last job ids, last spoken receipts), each with TTL and provenance, capped to a small token budget. Cache between turns and invalidate on updates.

entries.summary: Add a focus-safe execution coordinator around the existing FULL_CONTROL Mac executor. Before each plan, capture the foreground app and a lightweight accessibility/state fingerprint; route UI actions by explicit target app where possible without activating it; execute in bounded batches; after each batch re-check foreground app and target state, abort only on unexpected state drift, and return a receipt that records whether focus changed, what was verified, and which step remains. For actions that inherently require focus (typing into an unaddressable field), mark that requirement in the plan and restore the original foreground app afterward when technically possible. This is observability and recovery, not an approval gate.
entries.note: local-agent/focusCoordinator.js + focusCoordinator.test.js (22 tests); wired into orchestrateExecute; journal surfaces it on read. Prior note was empty. Before each plan it fingerprints the foreground (lsappinfo, ~14ms measured) and the target app's pid; routes ui_click/ui_menu/ui_find/ui_snapshot/ui_wait_for to the app the plan explicitly named so the AX API addresses it WITHOUT activating it - which fixes a live bug, since focusPolicy auto opens with -g while the owner is present and the next ui_* step then defaulted to app:'frontmost' = the owner's window; executes in bounded batches (PENDANT_FOCUS_BATCH_SIZE, default 4) and re-checks foreground + target after each; aborts only when a REMAINING step depended on what changed (frontmost-bound writes, or a target that quit/restarted) - an owner switching apps under a by-name plan is not drift; restores the prior foreground via 'open -b <bundleId>' in a finally, only when a step that could move focus actually ran, the app is still running, and the current front app is one the plan named. NOT A GATE: nothing blocks, prompts or waits; a test asserts no key matching approv|confirm|consent|authoriz|permission|allow|deny|gate|prompt|ask|await|pending|review exists anywhere in the receipt, and another asserts run_shell/send_email/delete_path run unconsulted. focusPolicy defaults untouched. Foreground reader is executionJournal.readForegroundApp (now exported) - one source of truth. Full suite 832/832 green.

entries.summary: Add a startup and periodic no-op input reachability probe to the Mac agent health path. When Accessibility is reported trusted, post the documented zero-delta cursor event (or an equivalent harmless System Events no-op), record the exact host bundle tested, timestamp, and result, and expose `inputReachability: verified|unverified|failed` in /observe and job receipts. Do not block FULL_CONTROL actions; instead annotate receipts and surface a warning when an interaction may have been a no-op.
entries.note: local-agent/inputReachability.js: posts the zero-delta cursor no-op at startup and every 15 min (PENDANT_INPUT_PROBE_INTERVAL_MS, 0 disables), recording status + host bundle (app Info.plist, else LaunchServices id) + timestamp. Exposed as $.inputReachability on /observe and per-receipt on input-posting steps (ui_click, ui_menu, type_text, press_keys, mouse_*, scroll, computer_use_task); /jobs/:id/receipts counts.inputMayHaveBeenNoOp. unverified strictly means NOT PROBED and maps to null in the inputPosting contract, so projectAccessibility still reports eventsPost:null when nothing measured. Reuses uiControl.probeInput and the existing ?probeInput=1 path, which now routes through the recorder. ANNOTATION ONLY -- nothing gates, and receipts keep the executor's own ok/status. No focus stealing; measured on this Mac, the no-op does not reset the HID idle timer. Measured 2026-08-07: com.aipendant.agent = verified (events post); the same helper run under com.anthropic.claudefordesktop = failed -- the per-binary point, live. Tests: local-agent/inputReachability.test.js (12). Suite 832/832.

entries.summary: Add an in-extension privacy boundary before browser results leave Safari: classify DOM regions and form fields (credentials, payment, health, private messages, identifiers), redact or hash them by default, and return only the minimum quoted spans/structured fields requested by the job. Preserve a local encrypted evidence map keyed by commandId so the user can later expand a redacted field explicitly. Apply the same policy to screenshots via local OCR/region masking, with per-site rules and an audit receipt.

Add a bridge self-healing supervisor with an explicit offline spool. When Safari stops heartbeating, mark the device unavailable, cancel/park pending browser jobs without 45-second request hangs, and have the Mac harness attempt a reversible recovery sequence (wake/open Safari, verify the AI Pendant extension is enabled, then wait for a heartbeat). Persist queued jobs with TTL, tab/session affinity, and the original intent; on reconnection resume only idempotent reads/watches, while surfacing any form-fill job as 'paused—review before continuing'. Emit a compact pendant notification and a Mac log receipt for offline, recovery-attempted, resumed, or expired states.

Add a typed discovery registry for granted tools and capabilities. When the orchestrator grants a tool, it registers under a stable name with a version and a canonical describe() entry so relay can reliably introspect and route without guessing names or relying on system prompt text.

Add a typed capability registry that maps discovered tool names and surfaces to stable internal identifiers. The registry should reconcile differences between what’s granted, what’s discoverable, and what’s actually callable, and expose a single describe(name) namespace so newly granted tools are immediately describable without guessing the right category.

For the wearable revision, add a small always-on audio/transport companion (for example an nRF5340-class low-power MCU with PDM/I2S and a ring-buffered codec path) between the microphone/speaker and the LTE modem, with a shared mailbox for sequence counters and loss beacons. Keep the nRF9160 for LTE and application control, but move Opus encode/decode, resampling, and jitter buffering off the 64 MHz application core. Give the companion a real fuel-gauge/charger interface and expose codec mode plus buffer depth to firmware.

Add a durable, crash-recoverable action ledger for every multi-step Mac/browser plan. Before execution, persist a plan manifest with stable action IDs, target fingerprints (path/app/tab), and intended outputs. After each step, write an observed receipt (including hashes or UI evidence) and a commit marker. On restart or reconnect, reconcile unfinished plans against current state: mark already-completed steps as done, safely replay only steps whose preconditions still hold, and surface a compact repair plan for ambiguous steps. Keep this observational and compatible with FULL_CONTROL_MODE—no new approval gate—while preserving the existing result receipts and undo endpoints.

Finish the implementation behind the granted mac_readonly_inspect interface for running apps, foreground app, accessibility state, UI snapshots, browser tabs, and approved directory listings. Add a heartbeat and stale-data marker so planners know whether a snapshot is current.

entries.summary: offline_alert_inbox
entries.why: Receives short, prioritized alerts from the relay (for example, a changed authenticated bill or fraud warning), queues them locally, and lets the owner long-press the single button to play the next alert over the existing speaker. The LED indicates unread count and an error/expired state; alerts remain available across a dropped phone/Mac link.
entries.note: firmware/nrf9160/src/pendant_store.c: alerts pulled from the relay are written to /SD:/inbox.jsn, survive reboot and link loss, and are surfaced on the owner's next button press — BEFORE any decision about the link, because reading them is a card read and a printk and needs no radio at all. Verified with the modem powered down. Source is GET /v1/state/pendant-alerts (device scope state:read, no relay change; /v1/announcements is admin-scoped and 403s a paired device — probed live). Cursor semantics, not set semantics: remember the last id and take everything after it, so a trimmed publisher array re-delivers rather than drops. Parses out of the SHARED HTTP response buffer, so the whole inbox owns no RAM beyond a 32 B cursor in the outbox manifest. The acknowledgement rides back out through the OUTBOX, not the radio, so 'the owner read this' also survives being offline: proven — read at 07:10:00 with the radio down, delivered at 07:16:26 as relay job_e8a8acc4 'Pendant surfaced 1 held alert(s) to the owner. last_alert_id=a1'. Also verified: three alerts published, a1 correctly skipped as already seen, a2/a3 held (inbox=2), a repeat poll added nothing. Deliberately NOT built, and this is the real gap against the proposal: alerts are surfaced as console text plus a two-flash LED, NOT spoken over the speaker, and the LED does not encode an unread COUNT. Speaking them needs relay TTS on a link that by definition may be down, or an on-device voice — a separate piece of work. Gated by CONFIG_PENDANT_ALERT_INBOX (default y, depends on PENDANT_OFFLINE_STORE).

entries.summary: offline_moment_bookmark
entries.why: On a short button press, records a timestamped local bookmark event (optionally a few seconds of low-rate ambient audio only if the owner has enabled it), gives haptic/LED acknowledgement, and queues it for upload when the link returns. The relay turns bookmarks into ledger events such as 'remember this moment' or a location/time marker; no speech recognition is required on-device.
entries.note: Same mechanism as skill-feb6116a, not a second one: a bookmark is an outbox item of kind 'M' with no payload, so it inherits the queue's durability, ordering, retry and drop-on-confirm for free. Judgement call recorded: these two skills collapse into ONE outbox with typed items; only the alert inbox (skill-20934f8c) needed a separate mechanism. Dropped from Button 2 (DT_ALIAS(sw1)) rather than a long-press or double-press on Button 1: any gesture costs several hundred ms of disambiguation on EVERY press to serve the rarer action, and Button 1 acting on the active edge is load-bearing for capture latency. Carries the modem NITZ wall clock, device uptime, and the link state observed at the press. Delivered device-scoped with no relay change: POST /v1/pendant/announce (format=bookmark) then POST /v1/pendant/jobs/<id>/events — probed live, /v1/announcements is admin-scoped and 403s a paired device. Proven on hardware: dropped at 07:09:45 with the radio powered down (link_at_capture=down), survived a reflash, delivered at 07:12:02 as relay job_cdbb858b with detail 'Moment bookmark held on the pendant. captured_at=26/08/07,07:09:45 uptime_s=98 link_at_capture=down'. Not built: haptics (no driver on this board) and the optional few seconds of ambient audio (a bookmark that records is a voice memo, which is skill-feb6116a). Known relay-side gap: a bookmark job sits in status 'transcribing' forever because /v1/pendant/announce always emits a 'transcription running' event.

entries.summary: offline_voice_memo_store_and_forward
entries.why: Records a short voice memo locally when the network is unavailable, then forwards it to the relay when connectivity returns. Provides a simple LED pattern to indicate stored memos.
entries.note: firmware/nrf9160/src/pendant_store.c (+.h), main.c, pendant_cloud.c: durable outbox on the microSD card. record_microphone() still journals to SD ONLY when there is no live uplink at press (the owner's standing rule: SD is the failure path, never the default); this adds the missing half — when the upload ALSO fails, the journal is fs_rename'd into a queue slot instead of being truncated by the next press, and is deleted only after the relay confirms receipt. Delivery is gated on a live WebSocket (the modem reports 'attached' while every relay socket times out), runs one item per idle pass so a press never waits behind a backlog, and is oldest-first with a 5-try ceiling. Proven on hardware: modem forced offline (CFUN=0 plus a socket latch, because the cloud layer auto-resumes a suspended radio before every socket), 30 s spoken memo captured with live_opus=0 sd=1, upload failed -115, held as /SD:/ob0.pcm 937500 B; device then REFLASHED (power cycle); queue recovered from the card (pending=2); memo uploaded autonomously with NO button press 12 s after the link returned; relay job_165a9c9a transcribed the actual words and the Mac agent replied 'Confirmed: it arrived late and was forwarded after the connection came back.' Cost: +312 B RAM, +6.7 kB flash for all three skills together, behind CONFIG_PENDANT_OFFLINE_STORE (default y).
